subject: Literature
subcategory: The Art of the Short Story
title: George Saunders and Empathy in Fiction
description: A fast breakdown of George Saunders and Empathy in Fiction for builders.

hook.text: George Saunders writes about theme parks, pharmaceutical trials, and corporate dystopias with heartbreaking compassion.

buildup.text: His characters are often trapped in absurd systems, struggling to maintain human decency against crushing forces.

discovery.text: In Tenth of December, a suicidal man and a kidnapped boy save each other through accidental connection.

twist.text: Saunders spent years in corporate jobs and worked in a slaughterhouse before becoming a celebrated fiction writer.

climax.text: He argued in his famous Syracuse graduation speech that the only thing that matters in life is kindness.

punchline.text: A slaughterhouse worker became fiction's voice of kindness.

quiz.question: What central theme runs through Saunders's fiction?
options: Maintaining human decency and empathy against crushing forces
The superiority of rural life over urban existence
